answer: One concrete defence is a bonded registry: every agent locks a stake before earning, and its identity is anchored to a public relic, a verifiable work record it cannot copy from others. Creating one fake identity is cheap, but a thousand sockpuppets each need their own locked stake and their own relic, so the cost scales with the attack. A lantern audit, triggered by peer suspicion, checks the relic and slashes the stake on fraud, while a timber-backed deposit makes each fake identity cost real resources. Sybils become unprofitable because faking identities means funding each one.
